title: The names soy hides behind
standfirst: Soy goes by many names on a label. Here is the list we read for you.

spans.text: The law makes a maker name soy when they put it in on purpose. It does not make them use the word you are looking for.

blocks.label: names we watch for on a label
blocks.caption: Counted only where the link to soy is settled. Names that depend on the product are listed further down, and are not in this count.

resolved.method: Names whose link to soy is settled, counted from our allergen registry.
resolved.excludedNote: 15 more depend on the product or are shared with something else, so they are listed separately rather than counted here.

sources.doc: Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act of 2004 (FALCPA), Public Law 108-282, Title II — soybeans designated a major food allergen
Food Allergy Safety, Treatment, Education, and Research (FASTER) Act of 2021, Public Law 117-11 — confirms the 9 major allergens (soy retained)

Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 on the provision of food information to consumers, Annex II — 'Soybeans and products thereof', incl. exemptions (a) fully refined soybean oil/fat; (b) natural mixed tocopherols E306 and natural D-alpha tocopherol/acetate/succinate from soybean; (c) phytosterols and phytosterol esters from soybean vegetable oils; (d) plant stanol ester from soybean vegetable-oil sterols
Soy Allergy — hidden-sources ingredient list (edamame, kinako, miso, natto, shoyu, tamari, tempeh, tofu, TVP, soy lecithin, MSG/HVP caveats)
Scientific Opinion on the evaluation of allergenic foods and food ingredients for labelling purposes — soybean (Glycine max) storage proteins and cross-reactivity
Food Allergies — What You Need to Know (guidance confirming FALCPA source-disclosure for flavorings/colorings and the highly-refined-oil exemption)

resolved.limit: We read what a label says. We cannot see what a maker left off it.

spans.text: These depend on the product. We treat them with care, and we say so on the label reading rather than guessing.
Names that look close but are not soy. These are the ones you can stop worrying about.
What we do when the label is unclear
If we cannot tell, we warn you. On this one thing we would rather be wrong in the direction of caution than quiet.
